content:
We have a task: build complete route of chemicals based on inputs. We have template search gave mapped_rxn and template_id 1914386. Apply_template gave precursors list: ['C#C[Si](C)(C)C', 'COC(=O)C(=O)CCc1ccccc1'].

We verified step is valid. Both precursors are buyable.

Now need to construct JSON route: root molecule is target. Need its SMILES. The target is the product from the template. The mapped_rxn shows product SMILES: "[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19].O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]"

The product SMILES is after >>: "[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]". Remove atom mapping numbers to get canonical SMILES. Let's convert: CH3 O C(=O) C1(/CH=CH/ c2ccccc2) CH= C1 Si(CH3)(CH3)CH3. So product SMILES: "COC(=O)C1= C(Si(CH3)(CH3)CH3)C= C1c2ccccc2"? Wait need correct.

Let's try to generate: Starting from mapping: [CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4]) is methyl ester? CH3-O-C(=O)- . Then attached to C5 which is part of ring: [C:5]1( ... ) [CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]... So it's a cyclohexene? Actually C5 is sp2? Let's just trust that the product SMILES is the target. We can use the SMILES from the mapped_rxn after removing mapping numbers and dot. The dot separates a separate fragment? The left side had a dot: "[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]... . O=..." That's the reactants. The product side is after >>. So product SMILES is as above.

We need to produce JSON with root type mol, smiles = product SMILES (canonical). Could we just use the mapped product SMILES with mapping removed? Provide as is maybe acceptable. The example uses simple SMILES. We'll provide product SMILES: "COC(=O)C1(/CH=CH/c2ccccc2)[CH]=C1[Si](C)(C)C". Let's verify: The product has a silyl alkyne? Actually the product includes a Si attached to a carbon of the double bond? The product includes [CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]... So a double bond to carbon attached to Si. So structure: a cyclohexene with a silyl substituent. The SMILES: "COC(=O)C1= C(Si(C)(C)C)C= C1c2ccccc2"? Wait the ring includes aromatic phenyl fused? Actually the aromatic is attached via a double bond: /[CH]=[CH]/[c]2... So it's a phenyl attached to a double bond.

Thus product SMILES: "COC(=O)C1(/CH=CH/c2ccccc2)C= C1[Si](C)(C)C". That seems plausible.

We'll construct route:

{
 "type":"mol",
 "smiles":"COC(=O)C1(/CH=CH/c2ccccc2)C=C1[Si](C)(C)C",
 "children":[
   {
     "type":"reaction",
     "template_id":1914386,
     "children":[
        {"type":"mol","smiles":"C#C[Si](C)(C)C"},
        {"type":"mol","smiles":"COC(=O)C(=O)CCc1ccccc1"}
     ]
   }
 ]
}

Check that second precursor is "COC(=O)C(=O)CCc1ccccc1". That's methyl 2-phenylpropanoate? Actually it's methyl 4-phenylbutanoate? Anyway.

Now we should verify route schema using verify_route.
